findings.description: A `.env` that passes `[ -f ]` but can't be read (for example root-owned with mode 0600) now blocks every Bash call. GNU sed exits 2 when it can't open an input file. Under `set -euo pipefail` that 2 becomes the assignment's status, so the policy exits 2. The adapter (`claude-shaped.sh`) treats 2 as "block", so every Bash call is blocked and stderr shows only `sed: can't read .../.env: Permission denied`, not a BLOCKED reason. This goes against the adapter's rule that "A policy that crashed must not block the session". The old `. "$PROJECT_DIR/.env"` failed with status 1 here, which the adapter turned into "allowing". BSD sed exits 1, so macOS is unaffected; there, a sandboxed `chmod 000 .env` turns off every git-safety rule, which is more than decision 34's 'Cost accepted' admits. A small fix is to append `2>/dev/null` to the sed call, or to test `[ -r ... ]` instead of `[ -f ... ]`.

The "runs nothing written into .env" test checks only that the marker file is absent. It never asserts the hook's exit status or stderr, and the adapter turns a missing jq or a crashed policy into exit 0, so the test would also pass if the policy exited before reading `.env`. Asserting `status` 0 would prove the policy ran.

"A value written with shell syntax, such as `$(...)`, is now read as text" is not a cost. It is the benefit, and it repeats the CHANGELOG sentence and the paragraph at line 1027. The real cost is the first sentence about `GIT_TRUNK` in `.env`. Drop the second sentence from the `Cost accepted` bullet.

The parser summary "strips one pair of quotes or a trailing comment" is loose against git-safety.sh: a quoted value is cut at the first matching inner quote (anything after it is dropped), and an unquoted value is cut at the first whitespace, not at a comment specifically. Consider "takes the value up to the closing quote, or up to the first whitespace when unquoted".

The line "The probe: sandbox-runtime 0.0.80 (tag `v0.0.80`, `626a596`) on macOS 26.6.2, 2026-10-18" does not say what was probed, and it sits as a source bullet in the Claude Code group though no claim cites it. Name the observed behaviour, e.g. that `denyWrite` blocks a sandboxed write under `.agents/`.

The reworded comment is accurate, but the inserted clause "Claude Code through the .claude/skills link when it is one" interrupts the sentence and "when it is one" is vague; "Claude Code reaches them through `.claude/skills` when that is a link" reads better.

The new `describe` defines its own `repoOnDevelop` and `commit` helpers, re-implementing the temp-repo git setup and the `spawnSync("bash", [ADAPTER, "git-safety"], ...)` runner that already appear in the file's earlier blocks; this adds another copy. File-level `gitIn(cwd)` and `runGitSafety(root, command)` helpers would let every block shrink.

refuted_findings.description: The new git-safety paragraph and its `Rejected: denying ./.env` bullet sit between the denyWrite paragraph (line 1021) and its Rejected bullets. Those bullets are `Edit(./.agents/**)` at line 1035 and the following ones. A reader now takes "Rejected: an `Edit(./.agents/**)` deny rule" and "Cost accepted: a sandboxed `git checkout`..." to belong to the `.env` paragraph. The git-safety paragraph and its bullets are interleaved with the denyWrite ones. The `Cost accepted` bullet at line 1056 is also separated from the paragraph it qualifies.
refuted_findings.refutation: The layout is real: decision 34 (lines 1010-1064) puts both bold paragraphs before one shared bullet list, unlike decisions 21 and 32. But it does not mislead. Each later bullet names its own subject: line 1035 says "Claude Code adds it to `denyWrite`", lines 1038 and 1041 name the `.agents/` hooks and `./**/.agents`, and line 1056 names `GIT_TRUNK` in `.env`. Blank lines at 1034 and 1043 group the clusters. That is a scanability nit, not a fix-before-merge defect. A low-priority tidy: put the `.env` bullet directly under its paragraph, or move the git-safety paragraph after the denyWrite bullets.
